summary: Built M2-S02 (access, design-only, owner metadata-builder) into nine files: four PermissionSet files, three PermissionSetGroup files, a two-type package.xml at API 62.0, and deploy-order.md. The design is the baseline-plus-persona shape admin/permission-set-architecture documents: one shared object-access set (Case_Agent_Core) carrying Case CRU, read on Account/Contact/Entitlement, create+read on EmailMessage, three field grants and three standard tabs, plus three thin persona deltas carrying only record-type visibility and the Severity__c edit. Every element name and enum value was copied from the Step 3 inventory built out of skills/admin/permission-set-architecture/references/metadata-examples.md sections 1-3 and 5, skills/admin/permission-sets-vs-profiles/references/metadata-examples.md, and skills/admin/permission-set-group-composition/references/examples.md example 1. All three declared checkers exited 0 on the first pass, the cited-skill checker for the manifest was also run at 0, every XML file parses, and check-outputs returned ok. No system permission is granted anywhere because the only Case-relevant one the cited skills name is marked UNVERIFIED; that and four other ungrounded points are recorded in deploy-order.md rather than invented.
confidence_rationale: Step 10: HIGH on four of five conditions - every emitted element traces to the Step 3 inventory, all three declared checkers plus check_deployment_manifest.py exited 0 on the first pass with no repair passes, check-outputs returned ok, and every declared output was written. MEDIUM because the fifth is not met and because of one extra file: three Questions-to-Ask rows were answered from a documented skill default or from a builder reading of requirement.md rather than from an answered clarification (expiry, step-up activation, and whether Billing may edit Severity__c), and deploy-order.md is written on every run per Step 5 rule 2 but this step's outputs[] does not declare it, unlike M1-S01, M1-S02 and M2-S01 which all do.

dimensions_skipped.reason: Three of the fourteen deduplicated Questions-to-Ask rows were not answered from plan.json. 'Should any of this expire?' and 'Does any permission need step-up activation?' (both admin/permission-set-architecture) took the skill's documented default - no expiry, hasActivationRequired false, the latter reinforced by that skill's note that group membership removes the session-activation requirement. 'Which objects does this capability touch, and at what CRUD level?' is answered at object level by Q9 but not at CRUD level by any clarification, so the levels were read off requirement.md (agents log and work cases; nothing grants delete). None of the three is a query failure.

Four elements the step could plausibly have carried were left unwritten because the inventory could not ground them: userPermissions of any kind (the one Case-relevant name in the cited skills, TransferAnyCase, is marked UNVERIFIED 2026-09-04 in permission-set-architecture/references/metadata-examples.md section 2); viewAllFields (API 63.0+ per the same file, against a 62.0 manifest); a tabSettings entry for Entitlement; and any MutingPermissionSet. Each is named in deploy-order.md under 'Elements this step could NOT ground'.

process_observations.observation: All three declared checkers exited 0 on the first pass and the composition checker printed exactly the output plan v5's acceptance-test description predicted, including the reuse GOOD line naming Case_Agent_Core across three PSGs.

check_access_model.py returns 1 on ANY finding, not on a severity threshold, so its score-100 zero-finding result over the four permission sets is a positive statement that no dangerous system permission and no viewAllRecords or modifyAllRecords grant exists in this step.

Case_Tier1 and Case_Tier2 carry byte-identical grants: the requirement separates the two teams by routing and escalation, which are Omni-Channel, queue and EscalationRules concerns in M2-S04, M3 and M4, and no answered clarification gives Tier 2 an access Tier 1 lacks. Both files were written because outputs[] declares both; the composition checker's near-clone heuristic needs four or more shared sets to fire, so it stays silent at this size.

M2-S02's outputs[] declares package.xml but not deploy-order.md, while M1-S01, M1-S02 and M2-S01 all declare both; metadata-builder Step 5 rule 2 writes the note on every run, so this step produces one file the plan cannot confirm through check-outputs.

The declared permission-set names Case_Agent_Core, Case_Tier1, Case_Tier2 and Case_Billing do not follow the Obj_<Object>_<CRUD> / Feat_<Feature> taxonomy that permission-set-architecture's SKILL.md points at in templates/admin/permission-set-patterns.md; the step's templates[] is empty, so no template was cited to resolve the divergence and the declared paths were written as-is, exactly as M2-S01 recorded for Case_Intake_Integration.

Whether Billing may edit Case.Severity__c is decided by a builder reading of requirement.md ('Severity 1 outages are 24/7') rather than by an answered clarification; the file grants Billing read-only and names the reading in deploy-order.md for the M2 gate.

admin/permission-set-group-composition has no '## Questions to Ask Before Configuring' section, so the deduplicated question list for this step came from two of the three cited skills; the composition decisions it would have driven were taken from that skill's examples.md and gotchas.md instead.
The step is built and its eight declared outputs exist; the molecular tests it declares have not been run by this agent.
